_what: Declarative watch list for the GENERIC Vast watchdog (.github/workflows/vast-watchdog.yml). Any Vast job KIND the engine implements can be watched from here; a kind it does not implement is REFUSED at validation time rather than silently watched.
_why_not_ternary_vast_watch_json: ternary-vast-watch.json is a LEGACY SINGLE-KIND list whose four entries are watching billed RUNG 2b legs right now, and ternary-vast-watchdog.yml already relaunches them. Reinterpreting those entries under a new schema, or giving them a second relauncher, would be worse than the gap this file closes. So the two lists stay DISJOINT, and tests/test_vast_watchdog.py asserts it: no unit_id may appear in both.
_how: The workflow runs on a cron. Per enabled entry the engine asks its KIND for evidence - is the result artifact present, is an instance alive, what is the monotone progress scalar, is there a recorded crash - and hands that evidence to the ONE shared policy in watchdog_policy.py: DONE / FAILED / RUNNING / SETUP_STALL / STALLED / DIED. Only DIED relaunches, capped per UTC day; a stall alerts, because a relaunch would hang the same way. Any alert also FAILS the job so GitHub's own failure notification fires.
_alive_is_not_advancing: RUNNING requires the progress SCALAR to have increased since the previous tick. A rented Vast box can sit up with a dead container or an idle GPU and look perfectly healthy. The scalar must be durable (in the object store, surviving the instance) and MONOTONE ACROSS PHASES - the paralogue MD job's simulated-ns counter RESETS at the metad->release boundary, so the kind ranks phases and returns rank*1000000 + progress-within-phase.
_capacity_refusal: A start answered {'success': false, 'error': 'resources_unavailable'} is NOT a preemption and is NOT waited out: destroy, add the machine to the exclusion set, pick another host. That policy lives in each lane's launcher/ops module and is delegated to, never duplicated here.
_relaunch_interlock: An entry may name an owning_workflow that ALSO re-rents dead legs. While that workflow has ANY run in flight - or cannot be queried - the engine reports DIED but WITHHOLDS the relaunch. Two relaunchers on one checkpoint prefix means two hosts writing one restart set, i.e. an interleaved trajectory that nothing reports.
_editing: Set enabled=false when a unit is finished or deliberately parked - do NOT delete the entry, so the history of what was watched stays legible. The engine is a no-op on an empty or all-disabled list.
_required_keys_are_enforced: Every parameter a relaunch OF THAT KIND needs must appear on each enabled entry, because the engine re-dispatches from these values alone. For paralogue_md that includes metad_ns / release_ns / n_rep, which do NOT key the checkpoint prefix - which is exactly why they must be recorded: getting them wrong resumes the right checkpoint and then runs it to the wrong length, silently. git_branch is required for every kind and is easy to miss: a schedule only fires from the default branch, so github.ref_name inside the watchdog is 'main', and without the recorded branch a relaunch would pull main's code onto a feature branch's checkpoint. Validated by watchdog_validate.py on every pass; an incomplete entry, or one naming a kind this engine does not implement, ABORTS THE PASS rather than relaunching the wrong thing.
